info.title: Arugula native client API
info.description: What a native client calls on control. Generated by scripts/api-contract.mjs: edit contract/api/native.json. Not a public API: it can change with any release, by adding to it (aru-076, aru-131).

2XX.description: Server-sent events, one JSON object each

x-arugula-untyped: the answer: {refused}, how many waiting mentions it settled
response: a JSON object built in place
response: a JSON object built in place
response: a JSON object built in place
response: a JSON object built in place
query and response: local to the handler

101.description: A WebSocket: Noise frames to and from the machine
A WebSocket: Noise frames to and from the machine

x-arugula-untyped: response: a JSON object built in place
query and response: local to the handler

deviceSignature.name: x-arugula-auth
deviceSignature.description: A device's signature over the request (crates/control/src/auth.rs). A browser-kind device's counts only if it paired as a native app, on routes marked native, with control's --native-clients on (aru-131).

AddDoc.description:
[`BOARD_DOCS`]' body: the Doc to link, a [`Pointer::Doc`] or a
[`Pointer::MachineDoc`] (a machine's agent links its own machine's), to
the board's strip, or with `row` (`row_…`) to that row.

AddMany.description:
[`BOARD_ENTRIES_MANY`]' body: exactly one of `pointers` (those items) or
`untriaged` (everything that matches, but the `except` pointers). More
than [`ADD_MANY_MAX`] is refused, 400: narrow the filter.

added.description: Rows made. An item on the board already isn't counted.

attached.description: PRs attached to the row of the issue they close, as a single add does.

AnswerAsk.description:
[`BOARD_ASK_ANSWER`]'s body: one of the ask's `option`s, or `text` when
it has none.

AnsweredAsk.description: An ask that was answered, kept in the row's history.

Ask.description:
A question on a row that a person answers on the board (Arugula #367):
asked by a person or an agent, or raised by the board itself from the
state of the row's items (`raised`, never stored, and with no answer).

asked_by.description:
Who asked, as a name: a person, or an agent and its machine. Empty
for a raised ask.

can_answer.description: The reader may answer it: the person it names, or an owner or editor.

mine.description: It is for the reader (a raised ask is for whoever reads the row).

raised.description:
The board raised it, from its items' state, and it clears with its
cause: nobody answers it.

who.description: The account it is for; empty for a raised ask.

who_name.description: Who it is for, as the reader's page names them.

Asset.description:
One picture of a Doc, without its bytes: the shape a machine Doc's
state gives (`DocState.assets`).

rev.description:
Changes whenever the name is written with other bytes: clients cache
a picture by `name/rev`.

oneOf.description: The work itself: a PR, an agent block or a run. It moves the lane.
Evidence that the work is done: a run or a link.

take.description:
For an agent block as work on a row another machine's block holds:
take the row over. The old block is folded under `earlier`.

block.description: A `Block` pointer's block as its machine last reported it.

live.description:
The item's state now, when the reader may see it: an item they can't
read says nothing, as an unreadable row does.

released.description:
A block that a newer agent took the row from (`take`): it is an
earlier agent whatever it reports, and holds no claim.

BlockState.description:
What a daemon says of one of its own agent blocks, and all it says
(aru-116's second ruling): the state word, the branch, the short HEAD,
whether it is pushed, how many files are uncommitted and the diffstat.
No message text, no file names, no prompts: the type has no field that
could carry them. This is the view, read leniently by a daemon; control
refuses a body with another field through [`BlockStateReport`].

title.description:
The name its starter or its person gave the block: a board's chip
for it. Never the first words of a prompt.

BlockWord.description: What an agent block is doing (aru-116's second ruling).

closed_at.description: When it was closed; absent while it is open.

closed_by.description:
The account that closed it; empty once that account is deleted. When
an agent closed it, the account it acted for.

closed_by_agent.description: The machine whose agent closed it, if one did.

created_by.description:
The account that made it; empty once that account is deleted. When an
agent made it, the account it acted for.

created_by_agent.description: The machine whose agent made it, if one did.

done_note.description:
What was done, written when the board was closed; kept when it is
opened again. Empty before it was ever closed.

goal.description: What the board is for, in a paragraph; empty means none.

lead.description:
The session that leads the board (#414): a post on the board's thread
reaches it. Absent when no session does.

progress.description: How many of its issues are closed.

source.description:
The tracker's epic it follows, when it was made from one (Plane's,
#483); absent for a board a person made.

BoardDoc.description: One Doc of a board: in its strip, or on one row (a row's [`Row::docs`]).

added_by.description: The account that linked it (the owner, for an agent).

agent.description: The machine whose agent linked it, if one did.

copy.description:
A machine Doc's copy on the platform (`pdc_…`), when it sits in this
board's project (native #673): the title and counts are then the
copy's, and the chip opens it while the machine is away. Older
platforms don't send it.

machine_name.description: A machine Doc's machine, by name.

missing.description: A project Doc that was deleted.

BoardLead.description:
The session that leads a board: the machine it runs on and its name there,
as that machine's daemon matches it (#414).

at.description: When the session took the lead.

machine_name.description: The machine's name now; empty while it can't be told.

BoardProgress.description:
A board's work, counted: the rows with a primary item (an issue or a
PR; a note row is never counted). `done` is those in the Done lane, and
`proven` those of them with a proof; `review` and `doing` are those in
the Review and Doing lanes.

BoardSource.description:
The epic a board follows: its children are the board's rows, and the
connection made the board, not a person.

connection.description: The connection that made the board, as the project calls it.

key.description: The epic's key in the tracker, such as `ARUGU-10`.

left_out.description:
How many children the board is too full to show, the oldest done
ones first.

started.description:
Whether the epic is started in the tracker (Plane's `started` group),
read from its mirrored item; not whether the board is open.

url.description: Where the epic is in the tracker's web app.

BoardView.description:
A board with its four lanes, in order (`lane_next`, `lane_doing`,
`lane_review`, `lane_done`), each with its rows, and its groups, in
order. The rows of a group are those with [`Row::group`] set to its id; a
row without one comes after the grouped ones.

chain.description:
The longest chain of open rows (`row_…`), first to last; empty when
no row waits on another (#762).

docs.description:
The Docs strip, in order. Empty for a board with none; an old client
ignores it.

groups.description: Empty for a board with none; an old client ignores it.

order.description:
Every row (`row_…`) as the board stores them: by group, in the
groups' order, then by position inside each, those with no group
last. A move that names the order it read (`seen`) names a group's
rows from here.

ready.description:
The ready set (Arugula #403): the rows (`row_…`) with an issue or a
PR as their item that are in Next and have no open blocker.

said.description:
What a write did that the board alone doesn't say: a PR attached to
the row of the issue it closes, an item that was there already.

sequence.description:
The rows (`row_…`) that have a [`Row::step`], by step, and inside a
step by what unblocks the most open rows, then by position (#762).

Category.description:
Where an item is in its own life, the same words for every source
(Arugula #405): Plane's state groups, which a native issue's and a GitHub
issue's open and closed map onto. A lane reads it: `completed` and
`canceled` are Done, every other category is not.

approver.description: The device that signed this; the device itself for the root.

noise.description: X25519 public key, hex (zeros for a recovery code).

sig.description:
Ed25519 signature by the approver over [`Cert::body`], hex; empty
until approved.

ChatAddMembers.description:
`POST /api/chat/rooms/{id}/members`: a channel's creator or its team's
owners add people of the team.

ChatAgent.description:
The agent that wrote a message (M197): the machine whose grant it acted
through, and its name now. The message's author is the machine's owner.

session.description:
The session that posted, as its machine called it then (#429): an
agent block's title, or the Claude Code session's name. Display
only; never what a permission rests on.

ChatAsk.description:
An ask's form (Arugula #214, [`ASK`]): which repo a thread's `@arugula`
works in, when the project's workspaces have several and the ask named
none.

asker.description: Whom it waits on, and their name now.

mine.description: The reader is its asker, so the buttons are theirs.

open.description:
It still waits on its asker: nobody answered it, and no later ask in
its thread took its place.

parent.description: The thread it's in (`None`: the room's own messages, an issue's).

session.description: The session its answer started, once it's answered.

ChatChannel.description: A public channel in the browser (#118).

members.description: How many of the team are in it.

ChatChannels.description:
`GET /api/chat/teams/{team}/channels?q=`: the team's public channels
(a private one only shows to its members, in their rooms), by name.

ChatFile.description:
One attached file, as the reader sees it. `url` is control's, for the
room's readers only (a session cookie, or an agent's token): the same
path with `?download=1` downloads it.

mime.description: What the bytes were sniffed as, never what the upload said.

width.description: An image's size in pixels, when its header gave it.

ChatFileKind.description:
How a file is shown: `Image`, `Video` and `Audio` inline (only types
that are safe to render: never SVG or HTML), anything else as a card
that downloads.

ChatFollow.description:
`POST /api/chat/rooms/{id}/threads/{seq}/follow`: follow the thread, or
stop. Answers its first message.

ChatGrantNever.description:
`POST /api/chat/rooms/{id}/grant-never`: the owner of `daemon` says its
agents are never to be asked to read this room (#578). What waited for
them is `not_granted` for good; a grant over the room undoes it.

ChatKeywords.description:
`GET`/`PUT /api/chat/keywords`: the words that notify this account as a
mention does (#114), lowercased, at most [`KEYWORDS_MAX`], each at most
[`KEYWORD_CHARS`] long.

oneOf.description: A team's, by name; its people are the team's roster.
Two teammates.
The thread about a pane, on its machine.
The thread about a session, on its machine.

An old conversation brought in from a machine, read-only (M124;
none come in since native #203, and those that did stay).

The thread on an object (M196), by its global id: a native issue
(`iss_`), a mirrored GitHub PR or issue (`fi_`) or a hosted
workspace (`hw_`). Its people are its project's members.

ChatLevel.description:
`POST /api/chat/rooms/{id}/level`: the reader's level for the room; none
is "use my default".

ChatLive.description:
What `GET /api/chat/live` sends, one JSON object per event (no event
names). Every event but `hello` has an id, so `EventSource` resumes
with `Last-Event-ID` after a drop, on whichever of the platform's
machines it reaches; a stream that can't be resumed (it fell too far
behind, or missed more events than control keeps) gets `resync`: reload
the rooms.

oneOf.description: First, once per connection: this stream's id, for [`ChatOpen`].
A new message: fetch it (`after`).

A message was pinned or unpinned, or a pinned one deleted (#119):
read the room's pins and the room again. (A topic changing is
[`ChatLive::Room`].)
A message was edited or deleted: fetch it again.

Reactions to a message were added or taken back (#104), or an agent
mention's status moved (#502): fetch it again. No room list changes with it.

A reply in a thread was written, edited, deleted or reacted to
(#106): read the thread again (the replies after the newest it has,
and the message at `parent`, whose summary moved). A reply also sent
to the channel is announced as a [`Message`](Self::Message) too.

The reader's own mark in a thread moved (another of their pages), or
they followed or unfollowed it.
A room appeared, changed or went: reload the rooms.
The reader's own read mark moved (another of their pages).

What a room of kind `object` is on changed (M203: a native issue's
title, body, state, labels or assignees): read it again. Sent to
those who see the room; an object nobody has a thread on has none.

An agent session whose card is in `room` changed (M257: a state,
a question, an answer on its way, a turn's result): read it again
(`arugula_control_wire::sessions::SESSION`). Sent to those who see
the room.

Someone is typing in a room (#111): shown for [`TYPING_MS`] and
never stored or replayed. Sent to the room's other readers.

The reader's sidebar changed (another of their pages; #120): fetch
it again. Only they hear it.

The reader's saved messages changed (#116: another of their pages
saved, finished or removed one, or a reminder came due): read them
again. Sent to that account only.

How a comment's send to GitHub ended (M205, Arugula #584): message
`seq` of `room`, a native issue's thread, whose post answered
`sending`. Sent to its author only.
Control hasn't had the machine's daemon's answer yet (#419).
A session took it (`session`), or the daemon didn't say which.
The session it named wasn't there (`asked`): it went to `session`.
No session took it: it waits in the machine's inbox.

The session (`session`) has it queued, but its hooks aren't
listening to take it (#571).

The session it named (`asked`) is there, but its owner silenced
mentions for it (#579): it waits in the machine's inbox.

The session it named isn't there (`asked`), or is more than one:
no other session got it, and it waits in the inbox. `names` are the
ones there are (#576).
The machine is offline, or didn't answer.
The machine's agent replied in the thread (`reply`).

Not delivered (#575): an agent's post, in a chain of agents' replies
or past the thread's rate limit. A person's message restarts it.

The session's turn that took it has started (#540): what only the
receiving daemon knows. Like a typing indicator.

That turn has ended (#540). An agent's reply, `answered`, usually
comes first and stays.

The session dropped it (#613): `why` says how. Final, like
`answered`, which it never replaces.

The machine's agents can't read the room (#578): its owner was asked
to let them. Delivered if they do; final if they said never.

ChatMentionStatus.description:
Where a message's `@machine` mention got to (#502), as control knows it:
what the machine's daemon said when it was told, and then whether the
machine's agent answered in the thread.

asked.description: The session the message named that the daemon couldn't find.

machine_name.description: What the machine was called when it was told.

names.description: With `no_such_session`: the names it could have used (#576).

reply.description: With `answered`: the number of the agent's reply.

session.description: The session it went to, when the daemon said.

ChatMessage.description: A message as the reader sees it.

agent.description:
Written by an agent on the author's machine (M197): shown as
"<name>'s agent on <machine_name>".

also.description: A reply that was also sent to the channel.

author.description:
The author's account, and their name now. Both are empty for a
deleted account.

deleted.description: When it was deleted: its text, quote and pane are gone.

files.description:
Files and images attached (#107), in the order they were chosen.
Empty for a deleted message: its files went with it.

imported.description:
Brought in from a machine's own threads (M124): the name it had
there. Someone with no account here (a tailnet login, an agent) is
shown under the machine's owner, by this name.

mention_status.description:
Where each machine's agent mention in it got to (#502), one per
machine, by name. Empty for a message that mentions none.

mentions.description: The accounts it mentions, and the agents (`machine:<id>`, M198).

parent.description:
A reply (#106): the number of its thread's first message. The
room's list has it only with `also`; the thread has it always.

quote.description: Lines the poster chose from a pane, copied in (decision 1).

reactions.description:
Who reacted with which emoji (#104), the first reaction first.
Empty for a deleted message and for archives brought in.

seq.description:
Its number in the room. Messages brought in from a machine (M124)
keep their old numbers, unless the room already had messages of its
own: then they're numbered 0 and below, before control's.

system.description:
Not something said but something that happened (#119): `author` set
the topic or pinned a message. Drawn dim and centered; never
counted unread, pushed, edited or reacted to.

thread.description: The thread of replies this message starts, once it has any.

via.description:
Posted for the author by a product (M237): a hud box's name, for a
review written there. Shown as "<name> via <via>". [`SYSTEM_VIA`]
with no author: a line the platform wrote (#122), shown apart, as
plain text.

more.description: There are more in the direction asked.

parent.description: With `thread`: the message that starts it, deleted or not.

thread.description:
Read the replies in the thread of this message instead of the
room's list (#106).

auto_join.description: Everyone who joins the team later joins it too.

private.description: Invite-only and out of the browser (#118); else public.

ChatNewDm.description:
`POST /api/chat/teams/{team}/dms`: the DM with a teammate, or (#117,
with `and`) with up to seven more, made the first time: the same people
again reopen it.

ChatOpen.description:
`POST /api/chat/live/open`: the room a page's stream has open (`None`:
none, or the page is hidden). Nobody is pushed for a room they have
open. A page with several chat blocks (#123) has several: `room` is the
first and `more` the rest.

thread.description:
The thread open beside the room (#106), by its first message's
number: replies in it aren't pushed for.

ChatOpenTarget.description:
`POST /api/chat/targets`: the thread about a pane or a session, or an
object (M196, `machine` empty), made the first time by someone who may
read it.

ChatPane.description:
A pane a message names, as the reader sees it: whether its chip opens
for them (they may reach the machine), and the machine's name.

ChatPaneRef.description: A pane a message names, as the poster sends it.

ChatPerson.description: Someone, as the reader sees them.

dnd.description:
They've paused their notifications (do not disturb, #115): a moon
on their avatar. Only that it's on, never until when or why.

ChatPins.description:
`GET /api/chat/rooms/{id}/pins`: the room's pins, the newest first,
as the reader sees the messages.

also.description:
With `parent`: also send it to the channel, as Slack's checkbox
does. The room's list shows it too.

files.description:
Files uploaded for this message (ids from `POST .../files`, #107):
the poster's own, for this room, not attached before. A message may
be only files.

notify_anyway.description:
"Notify anyway" (#115): in a DM, push the other person though they
have paused notifications. For this message only; anywhere else it
does nothing.

pane.description:
A pane the message is about: only one on a machine the poster may
reach.

parent.description:
A reply in the thread of this message (#106): the number of a
message of the room that is not itself a reply.

session.description:
An agent's post: the name of the session that wrote it (#429). Kept
beside the agent, trimmed and cut short; a person's post ignores it.

to.description:
In a thread (#647): who this wakes, chosen in the composer, in place
of the agent it replies to. Agents the text names come too. Empty:
nobody. Absent: as before this field. Ignored from an agent, and
outside a thread.

ChatPostTarget.description: An agent a message is for (#647), as [`ChatThreadAgent`] names it.

id.description: The machine's id, or a hosted session's `ses_` id.

session.description: The session on the machine, when it has a name.

github.description:
A comment on a native issue that's on GitHub (M205): what became
of its copy there, as far as it's known when the post returns. A
person's is `sending` then, and its end comes to them on the live
stream ([`ChatLive::Github`], Arugula #584). `None` anywhere else.

mention_status.description:
Where each machine's agent mention in it has got to by now (#571):
`sending` for one whose daemon hasn't answered. Empty for a post that
mentions none.

mentions.description: The accounts it mentions, and the agents (`machine:<id>`, M198).

pushed.description:
Whom control pushed (not those with the room open, muted, or pushed
for it in the last minute).

unreached.description: `@words` that named nobody who sees the room.

unreached_why.description: Why, for an `unreached` word that names a machine of the team (#572).

oneOf.description: One of the account's keyword alerts matched (#114).
A message in a room the person set to every message (#113).
A reply in a thread the person follows (#106).

A machine's agents, told over its connection (#394): the account
is `machine:<id>`.

ChatReact.description:
`POST`/`DELETE /api/chat/rooms/{id}/messages/{seq}/reactions` (and the
same under `/api/daemon/chat/` for an agent, see [`agent_reactions`]):
add the caller's reaction, or take it back. The emoji is the body of a
post and `?emoji=` of a delete. Both answer the message ([`ChatMessage`]),
and doing either twice is not an error.

ChatReaction.description: One emoji on a message, as the reader sees it.

agents.description:
How many of `count` are agents' (#632); the rest are people's. An
older control leaves it out, and it reads as none.

count.description: All who reacted with it; `who` names the first [`MAX_REACTORS_SHOWN`].

mine.description:
The reader has: a person's own reaction, or for an agent reading,
its own (never the owner's, nor the agent's for the owner).

ChatReactor.description:
Someone who reacted: an account, and the machine's agent if it was
the agent reacting for them.

ChatRead.description:
`POST /api/chat/rooms/{id}/read`: read up to here (it only moves
forward).

ChatRoom.description: A room as one person sees it.

archived.description: A channel its team's owners archived: read, not written.

last.description: The newest message's number, and the reader's read mark.

level.description:
What the reader is notified of here: their own choice for the room,
else their default for its kind (#113).

level_own.description:
Whether `level` is the reader's own choice for this room (else it's
their default), so the menu can offer "use my default".

machine.description: The machine a pane's or session's room is on, and its name.

muted.description: The reader turned its pushes off (`level` is `nothing`).

name.description:
A channel's name (without `#`); a pane's or session's room is
named `pane 2`, `session 1`.

others.description:
A DM's other people now, in account order (#117): one in a 1:1, and
a group DM is named after them unless it was renamed (`name`).

private.description: An invite-only channel (#118), hidden from the browser.

project.description: The project an object thread is in (M196).

target.description: The pane or session id there, or an object thread's global id.

team.description: The team a channel or DM is in.

topic.description: What people wrote about a channel (#119); empty when nobody has.

topic_writable.description:
Whether the reader may set the topic: a team can leave it to its
owners.

unread.description:
Messages after the read mark (not the reader's own), and how many
of those mention the reader.

wants.description:
How much of `unread` wants the reader: what a count of it says. In
an object's thread, its mentions, and on an open native issue
assigned to the reader what isn't from their own agents; the rest
of `unread` is only a dot on its row. In any other room, `unread`.

with.description: A DM's other person (for a group DM, the first of `others`).

writable.description:
Whether the reader may post here now (a DM whose other person left
the team, an archive, an archived channel: no).

ChatRoomAgent.description: A machine whose agents reach a room through its owner's grant (M197).

mentionable.description:
Whether an `@` of the machine's name reaches it here (#428): control's
own check when it routes a mention, not the page's reading of `powers`.

owner.description: The owner's account, and their name now.

powers.description:
What it may do here: `threads.read`, `threads.post`, and on a
native issue's thread `issues.write`.

sessions.description:
With `mentionable`: the names of the sessions its agents posted from
in this room in the last week, newest first, at most five (#428). Only
the room's detail fills it.

ChatRoomChange.description:
`PATCH /api/chat/rooms/{id}`: a channel renamed or archived, by its
team's owners; a DM renamed (`name`).

ChatRoomDetail.description: `GET /api/chat/rooms/{id}`: a room and who sees it (whom `@` reaches).

agents.description:
The agents a live grant lets read or post here (M197), for everyone
in the room to see: "Jake's agents on geek can read and post here".

can_manage.description:
The reader may add and remove a channel's members: its creator and
its team's owners.

people.description: Who sees the room: a channel's or a group DM's members (#118).

threads_unread.description:
Unread replies in the threads the reader follows, and how many
mention them (#106): the Threads view's badge, which the rooms'
own counts leave out.

ChatSaved.description:
`GET /api/chat/saved`: the reader's saved messages in rooms they still
see, the ones to do newest saved first, then the done ones.

ChatSavedDone.description: `PATCH .../saved`: mark a saved message done, or not.

ChatSavedItem.description: One saved message, with its room (the reader still sees it).

remind_at.description: When it will push the reader (or did: `reminded`).

ChatSearchQuery.description:
`GET /api/chat/search?q=&team=`: words (each a phrase, `mea*` a
prefix) and filters (`in:#channel`, `from:@login`, `has:quote`), over
the rooms the reader sees, or one team's; newest first, at most 50.

id.description: Made by the page that creates it (`s_` and hex), stable under rename.

rooms.description: Room ids, in the order the person dragged them.

ChatSidebar.description: `GET /api/chat/sidebar`, and the body of `PUT` (which replaces it).

collapsed.description:
Groups shown shut, by key: `starred`, a section's id, or a built-in
group's (`<team>/channels`, `<team>/dms`, `machine/<id>`, `archives`).

sections.description: The account's own sections, top to bottom, below Starred.

sorts.description: Groups not sorted by name, by the same keys.

starred.description: Starred rooms, in the order they were starred.

ChatSort.description: How a group's rooms are ordered.

oneOf.description: By name.
Newest message first.

ChatSystem.description: What a system line tells of (#119).

kind.description:
`topic` (its `text` is the new topic, empty when cleared),
`description` (likewise), `pin` or `unpin`.

target.description: The pinned message's number, for `pin` and `unpin`.

ChatTargetKind.description: What a daemon's thread is about.

oneOf.description:
An object, by its global id, on no machine (M196): only opened by
people, never in a daemon's reader list.

ChatThread.description: The replies to a message, as one reader sees them (#106).

following.description: The reader follows the thread. Always false to an agent.

read.description:
The reader's mark in the thread (a room number), and the replies
after it that aren't theirs (only while they follow), and how many
of those mention them.

repliers.description: Who replied, the newest first, at most [`THREAD_REPLIERS`].

replies.description: Replies not deleted, and when the newest was written (ms).

ChatThreadItem.description: One thread the reader follows, in [`ChatThreads`].

latest.description: The newest reply, for the list's preview.

parent.description: The message that starts it, with its [`ChatThread`].

ChatThreadRead.description:
`POST /api/chat/rooms/{id}/threads/{seq}/read`: read the thread up to
here (a room number; it only moves forward). Answers the thread's first
message, with its [`ChatThread`].

ChatThreads.description:
`GET /api/chat/threads`: the threads the reader follows in rooms they
see, the most recently active first (at most [`THREADS_LISTED`]), and
all their unread: the badge on the Threads view.

ChatToGithub.description:
A comment on an exported native issue, on its way to GitHub (M205): a
person's is sent as them through one of their machines, and waits as a
draft when none can; an agent's is a draft that waits for its person.
A person's post answers while its send is out (`sending`), and the
send's end comes after, on the live stream ([`ChatLive::Github`]).

sending.description:
Being sent now, through one of the person's machines: the end comes
on the live stream (Arugula #584).

ChatUnreachedWhy.description:
A machine's word that reached nobody (#572): its agents can't read the
room, and `reads` are the rooms they do read that the poster also sees.

ChatUnread.description:
`POST /api/chat/rooms/{id}/unread`: mark as unread from `seq`: the read
mark goes to just before it, backwards if need be (#116). The answer is
the room, as the reader now sees it.

ChatUploadQuery.description:
`POST /api/chat/rooms/{id}/files?name=`: the file's bytes are the body.
Answers [`ChatFile`]; it belongs to the uploader until a message is
posted with its `id` in [`ChatPost::files`] (an hour, else it's swept).
Agents use `/api/daemon/chat/rooms/{id}/files` the same way.

CloseBoard.description: `POST` to close a board: what was done, not empty.

DelegationRevoke.description: A delegation taken back: control may enroll nothing more under it.

Diffstat.description: A `git diff --stat` summary line as numbers: nothing of the files.

Doc.description: A Doc, without its sections: a list's row, and a view's head.

agent.description:
The agent session that made it as itself (aru-115): its `machine`
the session's id (`ses_…`), its name `Agent session <id>`.

author.description:
The account that made it, or "" once it's deleted, or for one an
agent session made.

machine.description:
The machine this Doc is a copy from, or null for one made here. A
copy is read-only here: the machine's Doc is the truth (#678).

machine_name.description:
That machine's name, when control knows it: null for a Doc made
here, or once the machine left. Older pages don't read it.

made_from.description:
For a team Doc made from a copy (Share with…): where from. Null for
any other Doc, and from an older platform.

sections.description: How many sections it has, and how many are written.

DocBoards.description:
[`PROJECT_DOC_BOARDS`]' answer: the project's boards that list the Doc,
open ones first.

DocList.description: `GET` [`PROJECT_DOCS`]: a project's Docs, the latest changed first.

writer.description: Whether the reader may make one.

DocOnBoard.description: A board that lists a project Doc.

rows.description: How many rows carry it as a reference.

DocView.description: `GET` [`PROJECT_DOC`]: a Doc with its sections, in order.

deleter.description:
Whether the reader may delete it: a person who writes in the
project, a copy included (native #673). An older platform sends
none; the page then takes `writer`.

writer.description: Whether the reader may write it.

DocWrite.description:
`PUT` [`PROJECT_DOC`]: what changes. `title` renames it. With `section`,
that section's body becomes `markdown` (and its heading `heading`, when
given); with no `section` but a `heading`, a section is added at the
end, written when `markdown` is given and pending otherwise.

oneOf.description: The person pressed stop while it waited in the session's queue.
The session's process ended in the middle of its turn.

EditBoard.description: `PATCH`: what to change; a field left out stays. An empty goal clears it.

EntryKind.description: Zone (a group, in a database; a lane, on the wire) or row.

oneOf.description: A group; `group` is read as this too.

agent.description:
The agent that wrote it, and the machine it was on (an id, and its
name when the machine is still there).

author.description: The person it's for: an account id.

id.description: The platform's id: `dft_` and 32 hex characters.

item.description: The mirrored item it's on, and its title, when the mirror has it.

native_issue.description:
The native issue it's for (M205): the issue itself (Open on
GitHub, `kind` `issue`), or one of its comments (`kind` `comment`).

ForgeItem.description:
A PR or an issue, as metadata: never its body. A Plane item (#420) is
one too, with `provider` `plane`.

id.description: The platform's id: `fi_` and 32 hex characters.

modules.description: The names of the modules a Plane item is in; its `labels` are names too.

number.description: A Plane item's sequence id (`ALL-2212` is 2212).

provider.description: `github` or `plane`; an older platform's items are GitHub's.

state_name.description:
A Plane item's state as Plane names it (`In Review`) and its group
(`backlog`, `unstarted`, `started`, `completed` or `cancelled`).

type.description: A Plane item's type (`Epic`, `Task`), when its project has types.

url.description: A Plane item's page in Plane.

project.description: The project's id (`personal` asked is answered with the real one).

withheld.description:
The project's linked repos whose items the reader may not see, and
why: their names are the project's, which its members see anyway.

Group.description:
A named, ordered section of a board that its author sets: a phase, a
wave, an area. A row belongs to at most one ([`Row::group`]); a group
holds no lane, and a row's lane is the same in any group.

progress.description: Its rows with an issue or a PR, counted as a board's are.

author.description: A GitHub login; a native issue's author's name.

created_at.description: When it came into the inbox, and when the item last changed.

item.description:
The item: `fi_` and 32 hex characters, a native issue's `iss_` id
(M202), or a run's `run_` id (M215).

project.description: A native issue's or a run's project (M202, M215).

repo.description: `OWNER/NAME`; a native issue's or a run's project's name.

room.description: A `thread_mention`'s room: the thread on the item (M202).

url.description:
The item on GitHub; a native issue's or a run's path on the
platform page (`/issues/<id>`, `/runs/<id>`).

InboxMark.description:
Mark an item's entries: `true` sets seen or done (now, if it wasn't),
`false` clears it, and one not given stays as it is.

reason.description: Only this reason's entry; all of the item's when `None`.

InboxQuery.description:
`inbox.list`: the reader's inbox, without what they called done unless
`done`.

agent.description:
The agent that opened it for its owner; or the agent session that
opened it as itself (aru-115), its `machine` the session's id
(`ses_…`) and its name `Agent session <id>`.

author.description:
The account that opened it (an agent's owner's), or "" once it's
deleted, or for one an agent session opened.

closed_by.description:
Who closed a closed one (an agent's owner's account), as its latest
`closed` event says: a list's row names them (UI audit #163).

closed_by_agent.description: The agent that closed it for its owner.

IssueAgent.description:
[`ISSUE_AGENT`]'s answer: the issue's thread and the message that asked,
and the session it started, if it did (else the thread says why, or
asks which box or repo).

IssueEvent.description: An event on an issue's timeline.

actor.description:
The account that did it (an agent's owner's), or "" once it's
deleted.

IssueGithub.description: Where an issue was exported to on GitHub (M205).

more.description: There are more past the last one (`before` its number).

IssueListEdit.description:
A change to an issue's labels or assignees: the whole list, or some
added or taken off.

reason.description:
Why it's closed (with `state: closed`): `completed` (when not
given), `not_planned` or `duplicate`.

IssuePatched.description:
What a patch made of the issue, and the events it wrote (none when
nothing changed).

IssueQuery.description:
`GET /api/projects/{project}/issues`'s query. Each that's given narrows
the list.

before.description: Issues numbered below this: the next page.

labels.description: Labels, comma-separated: issues with every one.

limit.description: At most this many (default 50, at most 200).

q.description:
Search words, in the title or the body: each one (`dep*`: a word
starting with `dep`).

JoinRequest.description:
`POST /api/join`. The CLI joins the same way, with only `cert` and
`proof`.

features.description: What the daemon understands, comma-separated (older ones send none).

proof.description: Its signature with the key it asks with (0.17 and newer).

team.description: A machine that belongs to a team (M19), not a person.

oneOf.description: A recovery code: approves a new device when every other is lost.

The desktop app's window. Its keys reach it through whatever
listens on the computer's loopback port, so, like a CLI's, they may
be a program's on that computer, not the person's. It connects and
approves machines, CLIs and other apps, but never a browser (see
[`Kind::certifies`]). Older readers don't know this word: control
leaves `app` certificates out of what it answers a client that
doesn't say it knows them (`app-devices`, see control's `compat.rs`).

Lane.description:
Where a row is, worked out on every read from the live state of its
items and never stored (aru-125). Each is the furthest that applies, in
the order `done`, `review`, `doing`, `next`.

oneOf.description: Nothing is under way, or the row is a note.
An agent block that isn't closed, or a run that is running.

A PR is open, or the issue is open and its PR merged (see
[`Mark::MergedNotClosed`]).
The issue is closed, or the PR merged or closed.

LaneSet.description: A lane a person set on a row ([`Row::lane_set`]).

by.description: The account that moved the row.

LaneView.description:
One of a board's four lanes as a read answers it, with its rows. The wire
and TypeScript still call it a zone (`zones`, `BoardZone`).

Live.description:
The item a row points at, as it is now: what the page draws beside the
row's own status, and the label of its link.

assignees.description:
Who an issue or PR is assigned to: a mirrored item's logins, a native
issue's names. A run has none.

category.description: An issue's status category; a PR and a run have none.

closed_by.description:
With `closed_with`, the words of the PR that closed it: `"(#12)" in
the title`, `"Closes #12" in the body`, `the branch feat/12-x`,
`attached to its board row as work`. Absent for a close from before
they were kept.

closed_with.description:
A closed native issue that a merged PR closed: the PR
(`OWNER/NAME#N`), so a wrong close is easy to spot (Arugula #743).

identifier.description: A tracker item's project key (`ARUGU`: the card reads `ARUGU-12`).

kind.description:
`pr` or `issue` (a mirrored one), `native` for a native issue, or
`run`.

labels.description:
The item's labels (#547): a native issue's, a mirrored item's, a
Plane item's. A run has none.

provider.description: `plane` for a tracker's item; absent for GitHub, native issues and runs.

repo.description: `OWNER/NAME` of a mirrored item; absent for a native issue.

state_name.description: A tracker item's own state (`In Progress`).

title.description: A run's: how it started (`manual run`).

url.description: Where a tracker item is, in the tracker.

LiveState.description:
What a pointer to an item, an issue or a run is now, from data control
already has (the forge mirror, the issues and runs tables): a separate fact, never written
over the row's stored `status`.

oneOf.description: A PR or an issue, open.
A PR, open, with checks still running.
A PR, open, with red checks.
A PR closed unmerged, or an issue closed.
A run, running.
A run that failed.
A run that is pending, approved, denied, canceled or expired.

MadeFrom.description: The copy a team Doc was made from.

machine_name.description:
The name of the machine the copy is from, when control knows it. Only
what the platform could tell; the copy itself is its owner's to read.

project.description: The copy's project (its owner's personal one) and its id.

Mark.description:
A note on a row that its lane doesn't say, worked out on every read and
never stored (aru-125, decisions 7 to 9).

oneOf.description:
The issue is open and a PR of the row merged, with none open: the
work is in, the issue isn't closed. The row is in Review.

The row's item was canceled (a Plane `cancelled` state, a native issue
closed as not planned or as a duplicate): the row is Done and never
proven, whatever merged.

An open PR of the row is stacked on another open PR: it targets that
PR's branch, so it waits for it. `repo` is left out when the reader
may not read the repo.

An agent block attached to the row (`attachment`) was closed, and
another may have taken its place: it no longer counts toward Doing.

The row is in Doing, every block of it that isn't closed has been
idle for longer than the project's `stall_minutes`, and no PR is on
it (Arugula #404). `since` is when the last of them went idle, in
milliseconds. It names no block: who holds the row is the block's
chip, for a reader who may see it.

The row's item is blocked by an open item (a `blocks` edge, Arugula
#403): the row stays in its lane. `number`, `title` and `repo` are
left out when the reader may not read the blocker (one such mark
stands for all of them: "something you can't see").

board.description:
The other board the blocker is a row of, when the reader may read
the blocker and it is on a board other than this one.

lead.description: The session that leads that board, when one does.

oneOf.description:
The row's item is in a loop of open ordering edges (Plane can make
one): it shares its `step` with the others in the loop.

Me.description: The signed-in person, as the hub knows them.

name.description: The name it chose, else its login, else "".

MoveDoc.description:
[`BOARD_DOC_MOVE`]'s body: the Doc it goes before, in the same strip or
row; none: last.

MoveEntry.description:
[`BOARD_ENTRY_MOVE`]'s body. A row moves to a group (`zone`) or, with
`zone: null`, out of its group; with `zone` absent it stays where it is.
It goes before `before` (a row of the place it goes to), last without
one. A group moves among groups:
`before` is a group, `zone` is absent. A lane is never set (aru-125): a
`zone` that is a lane is refused.

`seen` is the row ids of the group the row goes to, in the order the
caller read them. A row's `rev` doesn't count moves, so this is what a
move that mustn't overwrite someone else's checks: if the group's rows
aren't those, in that order, nothing moves and the answer is 409
`stale_order` with the group's rows as they are now ([`StaleOrder`]).
Absent, a move is made whatever the order.

zone.description:
The group the row goes to; `null`: none. Absent: its own. `group`
is read as this too.

NewAsk.description:
[`BOARD_ROW_ASK`]'s body: `who` is an account of the project. `options`
are 0 to [`ASK_OPTIONS_MAX`] (none: free text), and `recommend` is one
of them.

goal.description: What the board is for; left out: none.

lead_session.description:
With an agent's write: the session that makes it leads the new board
(#414). A person's write ignores it.

NewSection.description:
A new Doc's section: a heading, and its Markdown now or an intent for
later.

NotifyLevel.description:
How much of a room reaches the reader's pushes, and how its unread shows
(#113).

oneOf.description: Every message.
The reader's mentions and DMs.
Nothing: what muting was.

Pointer.description:
What a row points at. `None` is free text. The ids are the platform's:
`fi_…` (a mirrored PR or issue), `iss_…`, `run_…`, `hw_…`, `pdc_…` (a
project Doc).

oneOf.description: An agent block on a machine.

pane.description: The block's pane, as `%N` or `N`; stored as `N`.

oneOf.description:
An `https://` URL, as evidence (a CI page, a report). The platform
takes only `https`, no userinfo, at most [`LINK_MAX`] bytes.

A project Doc (`pdc_…`) of the board's own project. Only a Doc strip
or a `reference` attachment carries one.

A Doc block on a machine. `title` is a snapshot from when it was
linked, since the machine may be off; a [`BoardDoc`] reads the
machine's copy instead when the copy sits in the board's project.

PollQuery.description: The token the daemon polls with: `GET /api/join/{code}?poll=`.

team.description: The team it's the default project of; `None` for the person's own.

role.description: The reader's role in it: `owner`, `editor` or `viewer`.

hosted.description:
Hosted workspaces are open to this person (M179's allowlist): only
then does the shell offer to delegate a project to control (M178).
A platform from before leaves it out.

Proof.description:
The mark on a Done row that is proven. A Done row without one is not
proven yet.

pointer.description: What proves it: the merged PR, or the evidence attached.

ProofBy.description: How a Done row is proven.

oneOf.description:
A PR of the row merged with every check on its head completed and
none red.
A `proof` attachment.

PutEntry.description:
[`BOARD_ENTRIES`]' body. Without `id` it adds a row, last (`entry` is
`row` or absent), or, with `entry: zone`, a group with a `title`, last;
with `id` it changes that row or group: what is absent is left as it is,
and a change to `pointer`, `note` or a group's `title` names `rev`. A
new row's `zone` is the group it goes in. `kind`, and a `zone` that is a
lane, are refused, and so is every `status` (aru-125: lanes follow the work;
a question for a person is an ask, #367). The row's
`pointer` is an issue or a PR (or a link, for a note).

kind.description: Refused: a group has no kind.

status.description: Refused: ask with a question instead.

zone.description: A new row's group (`zon_…`); `group` is read as this too.

reason.description: A code a client can act on.

RelationDirection.description: Which end of an edge a row's item is.

oneOf.description: The row's item is the first end: it blocks, duplicates, was found from.
The row's item is the second end: it is blocked by the other.

RelationKind.description:
What an edge between two work items says (Arugula #403). Only `blocks`
gates: it keeps the blocked item's row out of the ready set until the
blocker is closed. `before` (#761) says an order and gates nothing; it
can't close a cycle with `blocks` edges.

oneOf.description: The first item blocks the second.
The first item duplicates the second.
The first item was found while working on the second.

The first item comes before the second, in the order the work is
done in.

RelationSource.description:
Who made an edge. `plane` and `github` edges are read from there, and
Arugula doesn't change them.

agent.description:
The machine whose agent added the row, if one did (it may remove
it; nobody else's agent may).

ask.description: The row's one open question: asked, else raised by the board.

asked.description: The last [`ASKED_SHOWN`] asks answered, newest first.

attachments.description: Work and proof attached to the row, oldest first.

block.description:
A `Block` pointer's block as its machine last reported it, when that
machine holds `boards.write` over the board's project.

docs.description:
The Docs linked to the row (#517): its spike or research, in order.
They move no lane and prove nothing.

group.description: The group (`zon_…`) the row belongs to, if any.

lane.description: Where the row is, from the live state of its items.

lane_set.description:
Set when a person moved the row and the work hasn't changed its
derived lane since (#494): `lane` is then the row's lane.

live.description:
A `fi_`, `iss_` or `run_` pointer's state now, when the reader may see the
item ([`BoardView`] is read with it; a write's answer has it too).

marks.description:
What the lane doesn't say, in a fixed order: `merged_not_closed`,
`cancelled`, `after`, `blocked_by`, then one `earlier` for each closed block.

proof.description: Set only on a Done row that is proven.

relations.description: The edges of the row's item, both ways, for the drawer.

status.description:
Kept for old clients: `needs_input` when the row has an open ask
(#367), `none` otherwise. Nothing writes it.

step.description:
Where the row falls in the board's order (Arugula #762): 1 plus the
highest step of the open rows that come before it, worked out on
every read and never stored. Absent for a row with no issue or PR,
and for a Done row. Doing and Review rows are step 1.

RowCandidate.description: One thing a row may point at.

assignees.description: GitHub logins for a mirrored item; account ids for a native issue.

labels.description:
The item's label names: a native issue's, a mirrored GitHub or Plane
item's. A run has none.

pointer.description: What a row takes as its pointer: `Issue`, `ForgeItem` or `Run`.

repo.description: `OWNER/NAME` of a mirrored item; a tracker project's name.

state.description: `open`, `closed` or `merged` for an issue or a PR; a run's own state.

title.description: A run's: how it started (`manual run`).

url.description: Where a tracker item is, in the tracker.

RowRelation.description: An edge of a row's item, as the reader sees it.

item.description: The `iss_` or `fi_` id of the item at the other end, with `other`.

other.description:
The item at the other end. Left out when the reader may not read it:
the edge is "something you can't see", with no title or number.

removable.description: The reader may take it off: an owner or editor, and it was made here.

RunDeployView.description:
The deploy a deploy's run applies (M219, UI audit #145): which, to
which environment, of what.

reference.description: The commit's sha or the artifact's digest.

RunEventView.description: One change of a run's state.

daemon.description: The machine that reported it, signed; none when control did.

detail.description: What its reporter said (an exit code, a reason, the pane).

RunLogPage.description:
A page of a run's durable log (M213: hosted workspaces only, kept 30
days).

end.description: The run has ended and this page reaches the end of its log.

kept.description:
Whether the platform keeps a log for it. Until it does, the run's
pane is where its output is.

note.description: Why there's no log, or what to do for the rest.

max.description: At most this many bytes, at most [`RUN_LOG_PAGE_MAX`].

offset.description: A byte offset in the log (a page's `next_offset`); 0 without.

tail.description:
The page that ends at the log's end as it is now, instead of
`offset`.

since.description:
The last event seen (`last_seq`): with `wait`, answer once the run
has a later one, or has ended.

wait.description: Seconds to wait for that, at most [`RUN_WAIT_MAX`].

RunView.description: A run, as the CLI and a machine's agents read it.

chant_ledger.description:
A release's entry in chant's ledger (M220, aru-098): a link to its
line on GitHub, which the platform checked is one.

deploy.description: The deploy a deploy's run applies (M219), as pages name it.

events.description: Its timeline, oldest first (left out of a list).

grant.description:
The standing grant it runs under; without one it waits for an
approval.

op.description: The S37 operation it runs (`arugula op v1`), and its SHA-256.

pane.description:
The pane it runs in on its machine (its `running` event says): its
live view, which the project's people watch end to end.

source.description:
Which spec, schedule or event: what an event's payload said is
untrusted text, for showing.

started_by.description:
The account that started it (an agent's owner's), or the schedule's
or rule's id.

started_by_agent.description: The machine whose agent started it.

workspace.description: The hosted workspace (`hw_…`) it runs on.

workspace_name.description:
Its hosted workspace's name, deleted or not (UI audit #145): pages
show it, with the `hw_…` id beside it.

Section.description: One section: pending (`body` null) until it's written.

body.description: Its Markdown (the machine Doc's: `chart` and `svg` fences draw).

id.description: The Doc's own: `s1`, `s2`, … in the order they were added.

intent.description: One line on what it will hold, shown while it's pending.

rev.description: Counts the writes to its body.

SessionAct.description: [`SESSION_ACTIONS`]'s body: what to ask of the session's box.

request.description: The open request it answers (the card's `open.request`).

SessionAnswered.description: An answer to what's open, on its way to the box.

SessionCard.description: A session as its card shows it.

answered.description: The answer to it that its box hasn't taken yet.

asker.description: Who asked, and their name now ("" once they're gone).

cancelling.description: Someone asked its box to cancel the turn, and it hasn't yet.

ci_rounds.description: How many CI rounds went back to it (M260), of at most `ci_max`.

ended_at.description:
When it last stopped running (done, failed, stopped): the clock
stops there. `None` while a turn is under way or queued.

harness.description:
The agent asked for (`claude`, `codex`), and the one its box ran
it on, once it took it (`claude` when the other isn't there).

heard_at.description: When the platform last heard from its box.

machine.description: Its box and agent block there, once the box took it: Open goes there.

merged_at.description:
When its PR merged (M265): the thread is done, and the session ends
once a turn under way does. Its card says "merged ✓".

model.description: The model its agent runs on, as its box last said (`Opus 5.5`).

model_asked.description:
The model it was asked to use (Arugula #215): its ask's word ("use
sonnet"), else its project's setting, else `None` (the strongest).

moves.description:
Where Move to… may send it (Arugula #214): its project's other
workspaces that have its repo, by name. Empty unless the reader may
move it (its asker, an owner or an editor) and it's queued or done.

needs_person.description:
CI failed again after its last round, and nobody in its thread has
prompted it since: it needs a person.

open.description: What it asks, while it waits on a person.

parked.description:
Done and parked (Arugula #215): idle long enough that its box
closed its agent, keeping its checkout and conversation. A reply
opens it again.

picked.description:
The one of [`SessionCard::tries`] kept, once one is picked; on a
sibling, its parent's pick.

ports.description:
Its workspace's dev servers (Preview), the public ones with their
URL.

pr.description: The PR its asker sent (M259): its URL.

pushed.description: A turn pushed its branch: its asker may draft its PR.

reason.description:
Why it failed or stopped, or why it's queued again (its box was
rebuilt).

role.description:
What it is (M264): `thread` (the thread's own, `@arugula`), `try` (a
Try 3's sibling of `parent_session`) or `review` (`@codex review`
of `parent_session`).

room.description: Its thread: the room and the message it hangs off.

started_by.description:
Who started it, when it was its asker's agent and not the asker by
hand (aru-121, a `sessions.start` grant): "<asker>'s agent on
<machine>", by their names now. The asker is still the asker.

tries.description:
A Try 3's sessions, on its parent's card: the parent first, then its
siblings, oldest first. Empty for every other session.

was.description: An `unresponsive` one's state before its box went quiet.

work.description:
The issue it was started on, with the first board that has a row for
it (#372).

workspace.description: The hosted workspace it runs on, and its name ("" once it's gone).

SessionFinish.description:
A turn's finish step (M261): the command, whether it passed, and when
it failed, the last of its output. A failed one isn't pushed.

SessionIssue.description: The issue a session works on.

SessionIssueLink.description:
The issue a session was started on, as its header's chip shows it:
`#N · ‹board›`, linking to the board's row.

board.description:
The board that has a row for it, when boards are on for the reader,
its title and the row.

SessionLine.description: One entry of a session's history, in words.

signed.description: Its box reported it, signed (else control recorded it).

text.description: What it says, in a line.

SessionMove.description: [`SESSION_MOVE`]'s body: the workspace it goes to.

SessionOpen.description: What a session waits on a person for.

options.description:
A permission's option ids, or a question's choices, by their labels
(Arugula #214: a button each; its own words still go too).

request.description: The request's id, as its box named it.

SessionPick.description: [`SESSION_PICK`]'s body: the session kept, one of the Try 3's.

SessionPlace.description: One of a project's workspaces, as Move to… lists it.

awake.description: Its box is up now (ready and online).

busy.description:
How many of its project's sessions are going there: queued, or a
turn under way. Not done or parked ones, which only wait, nor one
left from before its box was rebuilt.

SessionPort.description: One of a workspace's dev servers.

url.description: Its public preview's URL, while it's public.

SessionPr.description: A session's pull request, as its asker drafts it ([`SESSION_PR`]).

base.description: The branch it goes into: the repo's default, unless its asker says.

draft.description: Opened as a draft PR on GitHub.

error.description: Why the last send didn't get there.

head.description: The session's branch, which the PR is from.

template.description: The repo's PR template the body started from, by its path.

SessionPrSent.description:
[`SESSION_PR_SEND`]'s answer: the PR draft now, and GitHub's
authorization page to go to when the send goes through the browser.

SessionRow.description: A session as a wave lists it.

agent.description: The machine whose agents started it, by id.

head.description: HEAD after its latest turn, and when a turn last pushed the branch.

question.description: What it asks, while it waits on a person.

room.description: Its thread: the room and the message it hangs off.

settled.description:
Its turn has finished: it isn't queued or working, and no prompt
waits for its next turn (or it ended, or it waits on a person).

waiting.description:
What waits on the reader, in a few words ("its question", "a
permission", "CI failed again", "its PR to send"), if anything.

workspace.description: Its box: the workspace and its name.

SessionTry.description: One of a Try 3's sessions, as its parent's compare view shows it.

no_slot.description:
Queued with no slot on its box for it yet (the box runs three
sessions, done ones not yet parked too, or holds six).

turn.description: What its latest turn left: its diffstat and how its finish step went.

SessionTryAsk.description:
[`SESSION_TRY`]'s body: the harnesses of the two siblings, `claude`
or `codex` each (`["claude", "codex"]` when it's left out; a box
without Codex runs Claude Code in its place).

SessionTurn.description: What a session's turn left, as its box reported it.

finish.description:
What the workspace's finish step did after it (M261), when it has
one.

asked.description: The reader asked for it: only they send its PR.

may.description:
The reader may stop it and answer it: an owner or editor of its
project.

now.description:
The platform's clock when it answered, so the page can tell a box
that went quiet whatever its own clock says.

SessionWave.description:
[`PROJECT_SESSIONS`]' answer: the wave, newest first, and what narrows
it.

askers.description: Who asked for the sessions listed, `[account, name]`, by name.

labels.description: The project's issue labels, to narrow by.

tracker.description: The tracker it's narrowed to, when it is.

SessionWaveQuery.description: [`PROJECT_SESSIONS`]' query: each that's set narrows the wave.

agent.description:
Sessions this machine's agents started (aru-121); `me`, for a
machine's agents, their own machine.

asker.description:
Sessions this account asked for (by hand or through its agents);
`me`, the reader (a machine's agents': its owner).

going.description: Only ones going (not failed, stopped or merged).

label.description: Sessions on an issue with this label.

limit.description: At most this many (default 50, at most [`WAVE_MAX`]).

tracker.description:
Sessions on a tracker's issues, by its number: the tracker, the
issues its body names (`#N`), and those whose body names it.

SetLane.description:
[`BOARD_ROW_LANE`]'s body. `reason` goes with `done` on a native issue:
`completed` (when not given), `not_planned` or `duplicate`.

Status.description: Where a row stands. `None` says nothing.

UntriagedQuery.description:
Which untriaged items [`AddMany`] adds: a [`WorkQuery`] with `untriaged`
set, of the board's own project.

why.description:
`no_github` (the reader didn't sign in to control with GitHub),
`no_access` (GitHub doesn't give them access), `busy` (too many
lookups lately: it shows again within the hour), `unsure` (GitHub
couldn't be asked just now: it's asked again next time) or `no_app`
(this control has no GitHub App to ask with).

WorkItems.description: [`PROJECT_WORK`]'s answer: the newest first, across sources.

labels.description:
With `untriaged`: the labels of everything that matches `q`, `label`
aside (so the chips keep their counts), most items first, then by name.

next.description: With `untriaged`: the cursor of the next page, null at the end.

total.description: With `untriaged`: how many items match `q` and `label` in all.

WorkLabel.description: A label and how many of a query's matches carry it.

cursor.description:
With `untriaged`: the page after the one that answered this
[`WorkItems::next`]. Opaque; it holds its place when items leave the
list between pages.

label.description: With `untriaged`: only items with this label.

limit.description: At most this many (default 30, at most 100).

order.description:
With `untriaged`, `new` (the default) or `old`: by when an item was
last updated.

q.description:
Search words: an issue's title or body, a mirrored item's title or
mirrored content, a run's trigger (`manual`).

untriaged.description:
Only open issues (native and GitHub) that no row of any of the
project's boards points at.

ZoneKind.description:
A zone's kind: every zone a read answers is a `lane`, one of the four
([`Lane`]). No one makes a zone.

assignees.description: Accounts, each a member of the project.
